mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly negative at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 1% signals improved manufacturing activity and corporate earnings momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K units for three consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the median return is not significantly negative.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) decline over two months signals a labor market normalization, which boosts consumer confidence and earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically positive.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year decline in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 3% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative.
